# Risk register: starting entries (spec 23; HIPAA 164.308(a)(1))

Score = likelihood x impact (each 1 to 5). The live register, with owners, treatment and review dates, is on the **Compliance** page. Explained in [threat-model.md](threat-model.md). These are engineering estimates for the hospital's own risk assessment.

| Code | Risk | Area | Likelihood | Impact | Score | What reduces it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-001 | **Stolen staff password**: A password is phished or reused and used to sign in. | access | 4 | 4 | 16 | Two-factor for privileged roles, throttling, sign-in register. Planned: two-factor for clinical roles (D13), passkeys (HIMS-IAM-014). |
| R-003 | **Insider browses records**: Staff open records without a care reason. | access | 3 | 5 | 15 | Audit log. Planned in Phase 2: patient-level rules, chart-read audit, restricted records, emergency access review. |
| R-008 | **Secret or key leak**: Credentials reach the code, logs or a laptop. | data | 3 | 5 | 15 | Secret scanning in CI, gitignored environment files, encrypted secrets. Planned: managed secret store and rotation at hosting. |
| R-010 | **Data loss or ransomware**: Data is destroyed or encrypted by an attacker. | availability | 3 | 5 | 15 | Planned at hosting: backups, point-in-time recovery, restore drills, RTO/RPO. Until then no real patient data is entered. |
| R-014 | **Wrong-patient record**: Clinical data is filed against the wrong person. | clinical | 3 | 5 | 15 | Designed for Phase 2: duplicate check, identity header, entered-in-error workflow, two-person merge. Needs doctor sign-off. |
| R-002 | **Excessive or stale access**: People keep access they no longer need. | access | 3 | 4 | 12 | Least-privilege roles, 90-day access reviews, access ended on leaving. |
| R-009 | **Data sent to the wrong place**: Personal data leaks through logs, traces or email. | data | 3 | 4 | 12 | No query strings in logs or traces, hidden sign-in links, no clinical text in messages; tested. |
| R-011 | **Vulnerable third-party library**: A dependency has a known or planted flaw. | supply_chain | 3 | 4 | 12 | Hash-locked libraries, pinned actions, vulnerability scans in CI, Dependabot. |
| R-013 | **Missed legal breach deadline**: An incident is not reported on time. | compliance | 3 | 4 | 12 | Incident log with deadlines and alerts, runbook. Planned: drill. |
| R-004 | **Privilege escalation bug**: A flaw lets someone act beyond their role. | application | 2 | 5 | 10 | Default-deny server checks, escalation guard, permission tests. Planned: independent penetration test. |
| R-005 | **Injection or cross-site scripting**: Malicious input runs code or queries. | application | 2 | 5 | 10 | ORM queries, React escaping, CSRF protection, security headers and content security policy with reports of anything blocked (HIMS-SEC-012). |
| R-007 | **Audit log tampering**: Someone with database access alters the audit trail. | data | 2 | 5 | 10 | Append-only triggers, keyed hash chain, daily check; the app's own database user cannot change, delete or empty the audit log or touch its triggers (HIMS-OPS-007). Planned: external copy of the chain head (HIMS-SEC-016). |
| R-015 | **Going live before compliance is complete**: Real patient data enters too early. | compliance | 2 | 5 | 10 | This register; spec 27.5 go/no-go; legal items closed first. |
| R-006 | **Malicious file upload**: An uploaded document carries malware. | application | 3 | 3 | 9 | Type and size checks, no public links, sandboxed responses. Planned: malware scanning (HIMS-SEC-013). |
| R-012 | **One hospital sees another's data**: Data crosses between hospital deployments. | data | 1 | 5 | 5 | One database per hospital, startup environment guard, no cross-database links. Planned: isolation tests at hosting. |
